name: vodmal
description: AI-powered plugins for development tools by Dmitry Vorobyev.

plugins.name: vdm
plugins.description: SDLC workflow plugins: docs-sync (documentation synchronization), docs-distill (synthesis layer — the summary view nobody rebuilds because nobody asks; discovery + drift signal via `covers:` frontmatter, crystal harvest on cut, two-way handoff with docs-sync), learn (knowledge capture), changelog (project change tracking), crystal-* (multi-root workitem discipline gate — grow/bud/cut/cave/migrate with auto-scan + 4-tier status taxonomy + in-flight capture-reminder + orphan-sidetracks gate + batch legacy-doc migration + evidence discipline: Basis taxonomy, pre-action gate, live current-model section), intercom (central cross-agent/cross-session message store outside all repos, git-remote-identity routing + agent directory: auto-aliases + user-said names + description, SessionStart identity check, hard-stop on unresolved targets), wrap (pre-clean-session check: chat-only items written to their homes, one commit, a start phrase with a slug), retro (do the shared rules work: the owner's turns across every session on the machine, read against the rules each session received), and a lesson folded into the shared rules by a subagent rather than appended — the layer may be rewritten, a change to what sessions receive is shown to the owner first, and a writer installs it only over the version it was made from, with a history of the last 50.

plugins.name: vdm-git
plugins.description: Git safety plugin: blocks commit/push until user confirms, ships `git-guard-prepare` helper for file-based commit hand-off, enforces commit message format, crystal-completion backup gate, U+FFFD corruption guard on both commit surfaces.

plugins.name: vdm-comms
plugins.description: Meetings and correspondence discipline for repositories that keep them as files: a configurable contract linter for meetings/<date>-<slug>/ and series files (the contract is a floor distilled from three repositories — a track may resolve as a directory or a single file, index.md is owed only after the meeting has happened), with a project's own conventions switched on by name (comms.meeting-rules); meeting files split by who reads them — the agenda the owner's, the pitch what the counterpart hears, matched by topic name, with plugin templates for agenda, prep, pitch and index; a drift signal for the generated registry and per-track meeting pointers, written as markdown or Obsidian wikilinks with participant, topic and material columns; a PreToolUse guard that refuses to mark an outgoing letter sent — by creating it so or by an edit — without `sent-proof:` — the sending tool's id, checked against the access layer's journal of sends where it is installed, or the owner's word — and a PostToolUse check that names one a shell command left so, and a linted attachment checklist the sender can click; the form of an outgoing draft checked per its declared `channel:` (a subject line for email, a separator before the text to send — configurable per project, drafts only), and a draft declared outside comms/ named; each paragraph of a draft's text on one line, on every channel whose receiver keeps line breaks (all but comms.markdown-channels, intercom by default); a PreToolUse guard that keeps the raw .eml out of comms/ and the meetings tree, on Write and on a copy in Bash; who may write to a person and how to address them — `trust`, `addressed_as` and the From pairs in the HQ's people/, which a project without its own finds by asking the access layer for its HQ; and a pending-item summary — who owes what by when, series queues, unsent drafts, meetings without a transcript. The wording of everything it writes into the project is configurable (comms.labels), defaulting to English. python3 stdlib only — the frontmatter reader is vendored.

plugins.name: vdx
plugins.description: Unified lifecycle interface (up/down/build/test/check/fix/publish) + versioned maturity audit + AI bootstrap skill + how the agent is launched (vdx ai: session-start check, skill). MCP server: the installed vdx-mcp, else npx from @vodmal/vdx-cli on npm.
